narrative.overview: A map people trust outdoors, on a phone, in sun. It is plain, high-contrast and unhurried. The map is the surface; the interface is a sidebar on desktop and a search bar, chips and a bottom sheet on a phone, in the manner of Google Maps. Light and dark both follow the browser setting.
keyCharacteristics: Slate neutrals, one teal brand accent, four reserved status colors.
44px minimum touch targets, 12px corners, soft but not playful.
Light and dark from prefers-color-scheme; map tiles are inverted in dark.
Geist throughout; small, even type steps.

rules.name: The Never-Color-Alone Rule
rules.body: A status always appears with its shape and glyph, on pins, chips, list rows and feature tiles.

rules.name: The Reserved Colors Rule
rules.body: Green, orange, blue and gray are not used for decoration, buttons or links.

rules.name: The 16px Input Rule
rules.body: Inputs are 16px on phones so iOS does not zoom.

rules.name: The Floats-Only Rule
rules.body: Only elements that sit over the map get a shadow.

dos: Do pair every status color with its shape and glyph.
Do keep touch targets at 44px or more.
Do write every string in both English and Filipino.
Do use the semantic tokens (bg-surface, text-ink, text-muted, border-line) so dark mode works.
Do label desk-assessed data as unverified until fieldwork confirms it.
donts: Don't use status colors for decoration or links.
Don't rely on color alone to convey status or feature state.
Don't add shadows to elements that don't float over the map.
Don't hard-code slate or white utility colors where a semantic token exists.
Don't list places in a bottom panel on phones; the list is its own view.
